Subject: Marketplace partner data-controls check-in (residency / retention / deletion)

Hi David / Emily,

Thanks again for working with us on the CloudBridge marketplace listing. Before we finalize the listing copy and the partner onboarding checklist, legal and engineering asked that we align on three practical items about data controls so we can be explicit in the marketplace terms and the technical integration notes:

1) Residency / region pinning: can customers choose AWS/GCP/Azure region at subscription time? Do you enforce automatic cross-region replication for backups or is that optional per-customer?

2) Retention windows: what are the default retention windows you expect for primary data, logs/metrics, and backups/snapshots? Which parts can we scope per-customer in the offer?

3) Deletion semantics & evidence: when a customer requests deletion (end of contract or export+delete), what is the end-to-end process and expected timeline? Are backups and snapshots purged automatically or retained for a fixed grace period? What evidence/audit log can we provide to show deletion completed?

I attached a short checklist (residency-deletion-checklist-v1.pdf) that captures how Redwood typically phrases these items in partner offers — please mark up or reply inline with what works for CloudBridge.

Goal: we want to produce a short, one-page residency/retention section for the marketplace listing and a technical appendix for onboarding engineers.

Would appreciate a reply by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Rafael

Subject: Re: Marketplace partner data-controls check-in (residency / retention / deletion)

Rafael — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from the partner side; happy to follow up with our cloud ops lead if you want deeper technical notes.

1) Residency: customers select region at subscription time in our marketplace flow. By default we do not enable cross-region replication; we offer an optional geo-replication add-on (configured per subscription) which copies encrypted backups to a secondary region for DR.

2) Retention: standard defaults are 90 days for primary backup snapshots, 365 days for long-term archive (cold storage), and 30 days for operational logs/metrics. We can expose retention as a parameter in the tenant profile so RD and enterprise customers can opt for custom windows (within compliance limits).

3) Deletion: we support a deletion workflow that triggers immediate removal of live tenant data and marks backups for scheduled purge. Typical timelines: live data removed within 24–72 hours; snapshots queued for deletion and purged within the next snapshot lifecycle job (up to 30 days by default). We can provide a signed deletion certificate and an audit log export showing deletion events.

I'll run this by our cloud ops team and send any caveats — for example, in AWS if a customer has enabled cross-region snapshot replication it must be revoked before a snapshot can be deleted in the source region.

--

Thanks David — helpful. Adding a few technical clarifications / proposed contract language from the Redwood engineering/security perspective so we have a single source of truth for the marketplace entry:

- Region pinning: Redwood requires explicit region pinning in the customer subscription flow; we will surface the selected cloud/provider/region in the onboarding manifest and enforce compute placement. For marketplace offers we prefer provider-level options (AWS/GCP/Azure) plus region selection (e.g., us-west-2, europe-west1).

- Backups & snapshots: practical notes per cloud:
  * AWS: EBS snapshots and S3 objects are subject to lifecycle rules. If cross-region replication is enabled for snapshots or S3, deletion must remove replication configs first. EBS snapshot deletion is eventual and can take up to 24 hours to fully disappear from all APIs.
  * GCP: persistent disk snapshots are tied to project/region; deleting a disk does not automatically delete snapshots. Snapshot deletion operations are synchronous but admins should account for replication copy windows.
  * Azure: managed disk snapshots may be stored in the same or paired region; snapshot retention controlled via lifecycle policy.

- Suggested retention policy for marketplace terms (recommended language):
  "Redwood and Partner will delete customer primary data within 30 days of an approved deletion request. Backups and immutable snapshots will be scheduled for deletion and permanently removed within 90 days, except where longer retention is required by a customer's contract or legal hold. Audit logs relating to deletion events will be retained for 1 year for compliance and will be exported to the customer's chosen archive location on request."

- Deletion evidence: we can provide a signed deletion certificate plus a JSON audit export showing object/snapshot IDs and timestamps. For AWS we record S3 object keys, snapshot IDs, and lifecycle job IDs in the export.

- KMS / key management: recommend language that keys are customer-managed where required (BYOK) for enterprise offers; if partner-managed keys are used, both parties must agree to key lifecycle procedures for deletion/rotation.

Action items I propose:
  1) Rafael: confirm recommended contract language with CloudBridge (short one-paragraph clause + appendix referencing retained timelines).
  2) Sergio: I'll draft the cloud-specific appendix with concrete steps per provider (inc. replication caveats and expected timelines).
  3) Marissa/legal: review and sign off on deletion certificate template.

Happy to drop the appendix into the shared drive once I have CloudBridge confirmation on replication behavior.

David / Emily — really appreciate the quick turnaround. To summarize the agreed points and next steps so we can close the marketplace listing copy: 

Summary (agreed):
- Customers pick cloud + region at subscription time; cross-region replication is optional and must be configured per subscription.
- Default retention: 90d snapshots, 365d archive, 30d operational logs; retention is configurable for enterprise customers within contractual limits.
- Deletion: live data removed within 24–72h; snapshots queued and purged within 30 days of the next lifecycle job by default; Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate and an audit export (object/snapshot IDs + timestamps).
- KMS: BYOK supported for enterprise offers; partner-managed keys OK for standard offers with documented key lifecycle procedures.

Next steps / owners:
- Rafael: confirm the short clause below with CloudBridge and feed updates to marketing for the marketplace listing by 2026-09-03.
- Sergio: produce the cloud appendix (AWS/GCP/Azure) and upload to the Drive folder (attached matrix) by 2026-09-06.
- Marissa (Legal): I will redline the deletion certificate template and loop in Compliance.

Proposed short clause for listing (Rafael to confirm):
"Customers may select cloud provider and region at subscription time. Redwood and Partner will delete customer primary data within 30 days of an approved deletion request; backups and snapshots will be scheduled for deletion and removed within 90 days unless a longer retention is contractually required. A deletion certificate and audit export will be provided upon request."

Attachments: partner-residency-matrix-draft.xlsx (working draft) — Rafael / Sergio, please update with any provider-specific caveats (replication, snapshot IDs, object key format) before we publish.

If that all looks correct, I'll get legal to generate a DocuSign packet for the MQ addendum and we can attach the appendix to the marketplace listing.

Thanks again — looping in legal/compliance shortly.
